newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: NATO minister start enlargement meeting.
newsitem.headline: NATO minister start enlargement meeting.

text.p: NATO foreign ministers opened a meeting in the historic Portuguese town of Sintra on Thursday to start the process of selecting which former communist countries should join the West's defence alliance at a summit next July in Madrid.
The meeting comes two days after NATO agreed a landmark pact with Russia effectively removing its opposition to at least a limited alliance enlargement.

Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are expected to be invited to join the alliance, but Romania and Slovenia -- strongly backed by some of the current 16 alliance members -- are also pushing hard.
U.S. officials say Secretary of State Madeleine Albright goes into the talks representing a U.S. position in favour of inviting three rather than five.

The meeting is also due to review a reform of the alliance's command structures to make it more flexible and allow it to take on more Bosnia-style peace missions and review its current operation in Bosnia.
